_comment: What to read out of Mistral's one public price source.
MODELS come from `source`, https://docs.mistral.ai/models. Its index lists the
models currently offered as cards, and each card's page carries a machine-readable
price object with the unit stated per figure. Two more pages are read, for one
thing each: the batch discount, and the Voice Agents API's prices (see below).
PRODUCTS used to come from https://mistral.ai/pricing/api -- web search, code
execution, image generation, libraries, data capture and the two classifier models
were priced there and nowhere else. Mistral retired that page in October 2026: it
redirects to the docs site, and no page Mistral publishes states a product price
any more. The products are still sold and still billed, so they stay published,
sold-but-unpriced -- `unpriced_since`, with the last prices actually observed kept
beside the marker -- from the `products` list below, which is their whole inventory
now and the one thing in this file a human adds to. Adding a name publishes it
unpriced on the next run and reports the addition once; nothing is guessed at.
An earlier version read only the pricing page and silently missed four priced
models: OCR 4.0, OCR 3, Leanstral 1.5, and Voxtral Mini Transcribe 2 -- the last
of which the pricing page had dropped while Mistral was still selling it, so this
repository published it as withdrawn. A marketing page is not an inventory.
Models are not listed by hand. Which models exist is read from the docs index
every week; a model Mistral adds is published on the next run, one it retires
keeps its last observed prices under an 'absent_since' stamp. There is no
hand-written model list and there must not be one.
KEYS ARE THE NAMES EACH SOURCE STATES, lowercased: 'ocr 4.0', 'mistral medium 3.5',
'web search'. Not API model ids. Those are published beside them in 'api_ids',
read from the 'names' array the same docs pages stream, most specific first and
in the order given.
BOTH THE INVENTORY AND THE IDS COME FROM MISTRAL'S OWN PAGES, and from nothing
else. No other provider's data feeds this block, and it must never be made to: an
aggregator can confirm that a string is a real Mistral id, but not that Mistral
still sells it. Resellers lag retirements, and can hold contracts that keep a model
callable through them for months after it leaves Mistral's public API.
_comment_denominators: The docs pages state a unit per figure, as a 'denominator' string, split into
'input' and 'output' lists. The table below is the whole translation: an input
figure denominated '/M Tokens' is in_per_mtok, the same string on the output side
is out_per_mtok. A denominator missing from the table is NOT guessed at -- the unit
is part of the field name and there is no honest field to put an unrecognised
figure in -- so that one figure is skipped, the run reports it, and every other
'labels' overrides the denominator when a row names itself: GLM 5.2 states two
input figures denominated '/M Tokens', ordinary and 'Cached input', which would
A figure of 0 is skipped rather than published. On this source that is not the
ambiguous zero a broken parser produces: the pages state 'free' separately, so a
zero means 'this side is not billed' -- Voxtral TTS charges for the audio it
generates and nothing for the text it is given.
_comment_products: 'products' is the inventory of Mistral's billable non-models -- web search, code
execution, image generation, libraries, data capture, the two classifier models.
It is kept by hand because it is the only inventory left: the page that used to
list them with prices was retired by Mistral in October 2026, and no page states
a product price any more. The scraper reads no page for these: it publishes every
name below sold-but-unpriced, and the runner dates the state, keeps the last
prices actually observed beside it, and reports the transition once.
A name added here is published on the next run and reported once. Do not rename
an entry: a rename would publish a new product and freeze the old one, and the
name is the key a consumer already reads.
_comment_currency: priceUsd is read and USD is published. The source also states EUR, and the two
figures are genuinely different prices rather than a conversion of one another --
1.25 EUR against 1.50 USD. No conversion is performed anywhere in this repository.
_comment_format: A web page: asked for as HTML, and too small an answer is an error page.
_comment_batch: Mistral states its batch discount as a SENTENCE, not as a figure beside each
price: the batch API documentation says 'Yes, batch API is available for all
models' and 'We offer a 50% discount on batch API'. That sentence is the whole of
the evidence for the batch figures this block publishes, which is why they are
derived rather than read, and why every entry carrying one says so in
'batch_derived'.
'source' is the page the discount is read from EVERY WEEK. The percentage is
parsed out of it, never written down here, so the day Mistral says 30% this block
follows on its own -- and the day the sentence goes, the run fails rather than
republishing last week's rate as though it were still stated.
'fields' names the units the discount is applied to. A unit is in this list only
where Mistral's own batch documentation names an endpoint for it AND every entry
carrying the unit is an API model. That is what makes the list safe to apply
blindly, model by model:
in_per_mtok, out_per_mtok   chat completions and embeddings
per_1k_pages                OCR
per_1k_annotated_pages      annotations
Left out on purpose, though the same sentence would cover them:
* per_audio_minute. Transcriptions IS a documented batch endpoint, but two of
the models carrying this unit are realtime transcription models, and a realtime
model is not batchable. A missing figure is a gap; a wrong one is a wrong bill.
* per_mchars. It is what Voxtral TTS bills for the text it is given, and speech
generation is not in the batch endpoint list.
* cache_read_per_mtok. A cached input token already carries a discount of its
own; that the two stack is stated nowhere.
* everything a product is billed for -- per_mtok, per_1k_calls, per_1k_images,
per_call, index_per_mtok, train_per_mtok, per_model_month. None of them goes
through an inference endpoint, and the batch API is an inference endpoint. The
products are skipped by construction: their prices are frozen last-known ones,
carried beside 'unpriced_since' rather than stated by any page.
Do NOT add a unit here to 'cover more of the catalogue'. Every unit added is a
claim that Mistral batches it, and the source states one rate for the whole API,
not one per unit. Adding one that is not batchable publishes a price no one can
get, with no way for a reader to tell it apart from a real one.
_comment_voice_agents: THE VOICE AGENTS API is priced on one more page, `voice_agents.source`, the API
pricing page, in its 'Voice agents' section: a table of two rows, 'Mistral Small
4' at $0.04 and 'Larger models' at $0.08 a minute on 2026-11-10, under the
sentence 'Pricing for the Voice Agents API, billed per minute of conversation.'
No model page states these prices. Each row is published as a product, keyed
'voice agents (<row>)', lowercased like every key here, in
per_conversation_minute. The run fails if the section stops stating `unit`, if a
row stops reading as a price per `price_suffix`, or if the section goes: a rate in
a unit that may have changed is not published.
The page's other sections list the models by family, and the model pages already
price them, so they are not read. A section that lists no model and is not Voice
agents is reported in the run's notes: that is where a price Mistral adds -- the
products' prices coming back, say -- would show.
